risks.note: Explicitly tracked by management as a key external risk factor. Kaya's demand is discretionary, consumer-led aesthetic care, and the MD&A itself describes rapidly changing consumer mindsets - the move to preventive and personalised regimes, premiumisation and digital-led discovery - so a change in consumer preference directly affects clinic footfall and treatment mix.

Explicitly tracked by management. The MD&A notes the industry is transitioning to a more organised, technology-driven and experience-led ecosystem in which differentiation will be driven by clinical credibility, innovation and customer engagement, and that players integrating advanced technologies with personalised care and strong brand positioning are likely to capture disproportionate value - implying share loss risk for those who do not.

Explicitly tracked by management. Treatment outcomes in aesthetic dermatology depend on device and protocol technology (laser platforms, energy-based devices, regenerative and diagnostic systems); continuous technology refresh is required to stay competitive, making the business exposed to obsolescence of installed clinical platforms.

Explicitly tracked by management, with the risk framework designed to ensure alignment with evolving regulatory requirements. Kaya operates medically supervised clinical procedures and sells dermatology-linked products, both of which sit in regulated territory.

Management states the Company aims to scale leadership by continuously enhancing service offerings and strengthening technology capabilities; its stated competitive position rests on advanced technology adoption (for example Aerolase, MCT and Artiqa platforms) and standardised protocols, so a lag in adoption would erode the differentiation the strategy relies on.
risks.risk: Dependence on continuous clinical innovation and protocol adoption to sustain positioning
